Your descendants will curse you!

My descendants will be driving German cars.

That will never happen!
We will win!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative = to turn a blind eye to

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

+ acc. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to interrogate, question', paired with 'допрашивать'.

examples.text: Нам надо узнать информацию. Допроси его спокойно.
examples.trans: We need to find out information. Interrogate him calmly.

meanings.note: Declines like a feminine -а noun. Common masculine noun meaning 'uncle, fellow, older man' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: An unfamiliar fellow came up to us.
Speak, where is your uncle? Where is the commander?

ездить.gloss: to go (by vehicle, regularly), to drive

meanings.en: to go by vehicle (habitually or round trip), to drive, to ride
meanings.note: Multidirectional pair of ехать. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle, regularly), to drive'.

examples.text: И в сауну я не езжу.
examples.trans: And I don't go to saunas.

заговорить.gloss: to start talking, begin to speak

meanings.en: to start talking, begin to speak, speak up
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to start talking, begin to speak', paired with 'заговаривать'.

examples.text: Сейчас заговорит! В глаза мне смотри!
examples.trans: He will talk soon! Look me in the eyes!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: From Latin 'informatio' (conception, explanation, outline, from 'informare').

examples.trans: We need information on all the residents.

examples.text: В этой квартире нам нужны уши. Нужна информация по всем жильцам.
examples.trans: In that flat we need ears. We need information on all the residents.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Animate masculine noun. Common masculine noun meaning 'commander, commanding officer' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Speak, where is your uncle? Where is the commander?

meanings.note: A male child. Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'boy' in everyday Russian.
used to address a child you don't know
Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
of Germany; adjectives of nationality have a small letter
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to answer, to reply, to pick up the phone
meanings.note: Отвечать кому / на звонок. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'вечать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to answer, to reply', paired with 'ответить'.

examples.text: Я вам звоню, а вы не отвечаете!
examples.trans: I call you, and you don't answer!

examples.text: Почему ты не отвечаешь на мои вопросы?
examples.trans: Why aren't you answering my questions?

meanings.note: Colloquial figuratively. Common masculine noun meaning 'partisan, guerrilla' in everyday Russian.
Colloquial figuratively. Common masculine noun meaning 'partisan, guerrilla' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He keeps silent like a partisan.

examples.text: Вот партизан! Ну ничего, скоро всё скажет.
examples.trans: What a partisan! Never mind, soon he'll tell us everything.

meanings.note: Singular only. Common neuter noun meaning 'beer' in everyday Russian.
Пить чай = to drink tea. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drink', paired with 'выпить'.
used on its own: он пьёт = he drinks

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.en: to defeat, to beat, to win
meanings.note: 1st person singular is not used in standard Russian

Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Soft-stem adjective. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'следний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, final').

examples.trans: I'm asking for the last time.

meanings.note: Fleeting о in oblique cases. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'томок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'descendant, offspring' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мои потомки будут ездить на немецких машинах.
examples.trans: My descendants will be driving German cars.

meanings.note: Animate masculine noun in -тель. Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'атель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'traitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ничего я тебе не скажу, предатель!
examples.trans: I won't tell you anything, traitor!
The traitor revealed the secret to the enemy.

examples.text: Это ведь вопрос воспитания. Кого может воспитать предатель?
examples.trans: It is a question of upbringing, after all. Whom can a traitor raise?

meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'клясть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to curse', paired with 'проклинать'.
'один раз' = once, 'два раза' = twice

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with
meanings.note: мы сами разберёмся = we'll sort it out ourselves

В + prepositional. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sort out, to figure out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Смотреть на + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

TV, a film. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прашивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спросить'.

examples.text: Вот это что такое, я вас спрашиваю!
examples.trans: What is this, I'm asking you!

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.

творить.gloss: to do, to perpetrate; to create

meanings.en: to do, to get up to (something outrageous)
meanings.note: colloquial: что вы творите? = what are you doing?
Elevated. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to perpetrate; to create', paired with 'сотворить'.

examples.text: Он сам не понимает, что творит.
examples.trans: He doesn't know what he is doing himself.

examples.text: Самсоновы, вы что творите? Хватит, я прошу вас!
examples.trans: Samsonovs, what are you doing? Stop it, I beg you!

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.
